# Reload hides by default: the recreate fallback needs a host override

## Context

Operator ruling 2026-09-03: "reload => default action is recreate … MUST BE THERE BY DEFAULT."

Measured on a downstream workspace that overrides nothing: a focused pane's header carries `[maximize, close]` — no reload node at all. The pane implements no `dockReload()`, and the workspace overrides no factory, which is precisely the case the default is meant to serve.

## The Problem

The ruling is not new. It was given on 2026-08-31 and is recorded in a peer's session memory as: "reload must have a default engine behavior — recreate — rather than existing only for panes implementing `dockReload()`", with "#17966 is required default behavior, not optional polish." #17966's **title** carries it: "Default reload fallback: engine-owned recreate when a pane lacks `dockReload()`".

**Its six ACs do not.** They cover the two-phase transaction's safety only — phase-1 refusal leaves the live pane untouched, phase-2 preserves slot and action identities, destroy-after-live ordering, reconciler interaction after recreate, teardown mid-transaction. Every one was met, and the ticket closed legitimately via merged PR #17996 ("A user-triggered pane recreate amends the never-destroyed guarantee" — the ADR 0029 §2.6 amendment). **The ruling was never encoded as an AC, so nothing failed when the default did not ship.** That is the process half of this ticket, and it is worth naming: a ruling that lives in a title and a memory is not a gate.

What shipped is a consumer hook, deliberately and with documentation. The Contract Ledger on #17966 records `resolveFreshPane` as a "New consumer hook" whose fallback "returns `null` — recreate unsupported", and `hasDockRecreateFallback()` as "Prototype-derived — is the capability wired". #18014 AC-7 then scoped the factory to a single host: "Workstation's fresh-pane factory bypasses `paneCache` … `resolveFreshPane` always creates independently."

So a workspace that overrides nothing has no recreate capability, and `syncDockReloadAction` correctly hides reload.

The consumer-hook rationale is real and must survive any fix. From the hook's own JSDoc: an option on `resolvePane` "would be silently ignored and hand back **the very instance the recreate is meant to replace**." A distinct hook cannot be accidentally satisfied by a cache. The open question is therefore not "remove the hook" but **"what can the engine mint without one"**.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:3651` — `resolveFreshPane(itemId, item) { return null }`, the honest declining default.
- `:3671` — `hasDockRecreateFallback() { return this.resolveFreshPane !== Workspace.prototype.resolveFreshPane }`. Prototype identity, so the base implementation is excluded **by construction**: the engine can never be its own fallback under this predicate.
- `Workspace#syncDockReloadAction` — `hidden = typeof carrier !== 'function' && !this.hasDockRecreateFallback()`; hides only when neither delegation nor fallback can serve the item.
- `LayoutAdapter.mjs` projects reload with a CONSTANT `hidden: true` (stable-instance discipline), revealed only by that post-settle sweep.
- Withdrawn actions carry no DOM node (#18015), so the absence is invisible to inspection.

## The Fix

Give the engine a default `resolveFreshPane` that mints a pane from the item's own persisted record — `item` is already the hook's second argument — so `hasDockRecreateFallback()` answers `true` without a host override, while a host override stays authoritative and `dockReload()` delegation keeps priority.

The design question to answer before implementing: **what does the engine recreate FROM?** The item catalog record, versus the pane's own config snapshot, versus a `module` reference. Whichever is chosen must not resolve through any live-instance cache — that is the exact trap the current hook shape exists to prevent — and `hasDockRecreateFallback()` must stop being prototype-identity-derived once the base can serve.

| `Workspace#resolveFreshPane` | `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:3651` | engine default mints from the item record instead of returning `null` | a host override wins unchanged | JSDoc | identity arm: the minted pane is never the live instance |
| `Workspace#hasDockRecreateFallback` | `:3671` | no longer prototype-identity-derived; `true` when the base can serve | `false` only if the engine genuinely cannot mint | JSDoc | visibility arm on a bare workspace |

| ADR 0029 §2.6 | `learn/agentos/decisions/0029-docking-design.md` | unchanged — user-triggered only; automatic recreation still forbidden | — | the record | existing amendment stands |

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029 §2.6` — the user-triggered recreate exception already exists and is conditioned on the two-phase guarantee; this ticket widens who can serve it, not when it may run. Successor to #17966 (closed, PR merged): not a reopen.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 A `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace` subclass that overrides nothing projects a reachable `reload` on a focused pane whose card implements no `dockReload()`.
- [ ] AC-2 The engine's default recreate mints a pane that is **not** the live instance it replaces, proven by identity — #17966's `live-instance` refusal stays red-proof.
- [ ] AC-3 A host override of `resolveFreshPane` still wins, and `dockReload()` delegation still preempts recreate; both mutation-proven, with #17966's delegation-priority arm green.
- [ ] AC-4 Every #17966 transaction guarantee holds on the engine-owned path: phase-1 refusal leaves the live pane untouched, phase-2 preserves slot/tab/header/action/overflow identities, destroy happens only after the candidate is live, teardown mid-transaction settles without leaks.
- [ ] AC-5 A declining item still shows the action and settles with a named refusal rather than hiding the button — the shipped behaviour the #17966 ledger records ("hiding would leave a wedged pane with no affordance").
- [ ] AC-6 Red-first witness at the current head asserting reload's presence on a bare workspace; absence asserted as **node presence**, not display.
- [ ] AC-7 Exact-head unit + component suites green.

## Out of Scope

- Lock and pop-out defaults — the sibling successor filed alongside this one.
- Automatic (non-user-triggered) recreation: still forbidden by ADR 0029 §2.6.
- Changing what `dockReload()` means for panes that implement it.

## Avoided Traps

- **Reopening #17966.** Its ACs were met and it had a merged PR. The gap is that the ruling lived in the title rather than in an AC — a successor is the correct instrument.
- **Serving recreate through an option on `resolvePane`.** Named and rejected in the hook's own JSDoc: consumers that do not implement it hand back the cached instance the recreate exists to replace, silently.
- **Leaving capability derived from prototype identity once a base exists.** The predicate would answer `false` for every consumer while the engine can in fact serve — the defect this ticket is about, one layer up.

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-09-02T22:56:01Z

Closing as **superseded by #18151**, together with its sibling #18148.

This ticket was right about the mechanism and wrong about the scope. `hasDockRecreateFallback()` returning `this.resolveFreshPane !== Workspace.prototype.resolveFreshPane` does mean the engine can never be its own fallback by construction, and the base `resolveFreshPane` returning `null` does mean reload hides for every pane without a `dockReload()` method. But that is one of three seams with the same shape, and fixing it alone would have left the pattern to reappear at the next hook.

The finding worth keeping, and now recorded in #18151: the operator ruled on 2026-08-31 that recreate must be the engine default. It reached #17966's **title** and a peer's session memory, and never became an AC — so #17966 closed legitimately on six transaction-safety ACs, all met, while the default it existed to deliver never shipped. Nothing failed, because nothing encoded it. A ruling that lives in a title is not a gate.

The consumer-hook rationale from the #17966 ledger stands and constrains any successor: an option on `resolvePane` "would be silently ignored and hand back the very instance the recreate is meant to replace", so a distinct hook cannot be accidentally satisfied by a cache. The successor question is therefore not "remove the hook" but "what can the engine mint without one" — the item record it already persisted is the candidate, and `hasDockRecreateFallback()` must stop being prototype-identity-derived once a base can serve.

Carried into #18151's problem scope and intended-solution shape. No PR was opened against this ticket, so this is a clean supersede rather than a reopen-and-retarget.
